name: Alex Rivera
learnings: Concrete pricing examples outperform generic startup advice.

First-person pricing experiments framed as a specific numeric change plus a counterintuitive result ("I tripled my price, nobody left") beat baseline ~2.3x with 81% retention. The hook pattern has three reusable parts: first person, a hard number, and a payoff that cannot be resolved from the title. Retention data shows viewers stay for the mechanism, not the outcome — so the follow-up should deliver the "how" (the actual email, the actual spreadsheet) as a reproduced artifact. Untested: whether the lift came from the pricing topic or the hook structure; applying the same structure to a distribution moment would separate the two.
